subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: For non-group, not-from-me iMessage DMs where sender canonicalizes to `destination_caller_id`, should OpenClaw only repair when a canonical peer is recoverable, or also drop fail-closed when no peer can be recovered before access control?
rationale: That choice controls whether ambiguous local-sender payloads can reach authorization, pairing, routing, and reply delivery, so it is a security-boundary policy decision rather than a purely mechanical refactor.

options.title: Repair Confident Canonical Peers
options.body: Require canonical `normalizeIMessageHandle` comparisons, repair only when a distinct peer is found, and require live after-fix proof before merge.

options.title: Add A Fail-Closed Guard
options.body: Repair confident peers and drop ambiguous local-sender DMs before access control when the peer cannot be recovered safely.

options.title: Pause Until Root Cause Is Clear
options.body: If the author's remaining failure is not this sender-fallback race, pause this branch and track the narrower iMessage identity bug separately.

recommendation.title: Repair Confident Canonical Peers
recommendation.body: Require canonical `normalizeIMessageHandle` comparisons, repair only when a distinct peer is found, and require live after-fix proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged `destination_caller_id` self-chat classification work is the closest history for the ambiguous sender-vs-destination security decision.
